scope: Read-only audit of frozen formal baseline runners, locally archived papers/author sources, protocols, source bindings, and completed outputs. No internet, training, test-set access, or baseline mutation.

overall.safe_publication_claim: Three formal transferred baselines; Lookback and GHOST are paper-structure transfers, while LUMINA is an official-code-formula transfer. None is an end-to-end official reproduction.

preserved: risk OR label equivalent to author minimum factual label
unweighted span mean over all 32x32 layer-head features
LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000) with all other sklearn defaults
no scaler, sample/class weights, C search, fusion, or smoothing

differences.item: Only author step03 is locally archived and hashed; attention extraction is a custom local implementation and author step01 is not locally auditable.
Local predictor timing and assistant-header allocation are explicit conventions whose exact equality to author extraction is not established.
NF4/BF16 teacher-forced replay and 3046 cross-generator responses replace native author generation traces.
Material-group 3680/159 split replaces author random/two-fold evaluation.
Fit-threshold window F1 and answer-max F1 are local evaluation adaptations; native paper comparison is 8-BPE span AUROC.

preserved: unweighted mean over all answer tokens
RandomForestClassifier with 750 trees, depth 40, split 8, leaf 2, sqrt, balanced_subsample
whole-answer output only; token/window output is N/A
no scaler, external weight, projection, fusion, or smoothing

differences.item: No official author code is available; feature extraction is locally reconstructed from the paper.
Pre-token P+i-1 timing, HF states 3..29, and final-state convention are local executable choices not resolved by the paper.
Llama2-7B-chat NF4 is outside the paper's four reported GHOST backbones; expanded answers are proxy replays.
The final published RF parameters are used directly; the paper's 50-configuration five-fold RandomizedSearchCV is not rerun, and seed 42 is local.
The same 159 calibration answers select and report the F1 threshold; the paper's validation threshold procedure is underspecified.

completed_result.prediction_behavior: all 159 calibration answers predicted risk at selected threshold

preserved: cosine-kernel MMD with algebraically equivalent streaming reduction
official-code all-output-layer convention including repeated final norm
same answer token IDs under original and random contexts
no classifier fit, coefficient search, fusion, smoothing, sigmoid, clipping, or normalization
diagnostic probability columns excluded from baseline score

differences.item: Pinned official code includes the final output state and repeats final norm, while paper Eq.8 ends at L-1; this transfer follows code.
Random-document assignment and full evidence-block replacement are local deterministic data interventions.
Frozen prompt IDs omit official extra-space retokenization and 12000-character truncation.
NF4/BF16 model replay with FP32 vocabulary projection, softmax, and streaming reductions is mathematically checked but not bitwise official execution.
Four-BPE window means and answer-max are local localization adaptations; paper-native response aggregation is the all-token mean stored separately.

forbidden_claims: complete formal result before 3839 records validate
four-BPE answer-max as paper-native LUMINA aggregation

documentation_findings.item: FORMAL_BASELINE_FREEZE.md freezes only the final Lookback/GHOST runners, while their formal identity also depends on upstream local feature extractors. Existing source bindings currently protect the completed artifacts.
The LUMINA freeze omits hashes for the thin formula adapter, memory-bounded port, and archived official source; signature.json currently binds them.
BASELINE_PROTOCOL.md cites Lookback step01 but no local step01 snapshot/hash was found; only step03 is locally locked.
Lookback answer-max and LUMINA window/answer-max readouts are already disclosed as evaluation adaptations and must remain separate from author-native outputs.
